q-26935.name: Question 1
q-26935.problem: The point $P$ with coordinates $(8,12)$ lies on the curve $y=f(x).$ Which of the following points must lie on $y=2f(x)?$
q-26935.worked_solution:
The function $y=2f(x)$ represents a stretch of the function $y=f(x)$ by a factor of $2$ parallel to the $y$-axis. This has the effect of multiplying the $y$-coordinates of all points on $y=f(x)$ by $2.$

Therefore, the point $(8,12)$ on $f(x)$ is mapped to the point $(8,2\cdot 12)=(8,24),$ and this point must lie on the graph of $y=2f(x).$

q-26935.html:
Question 1
?

The point P with coordinates (8,12) lies on the curve y=f(x). Which of the following points must lie on y=2f(x)?

a
(8,12)
b
(16,12)
c
(8,24)
d
(16,24)
e
(8,6)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The function y=2f(x) represents a stretch of the function y=f(x) by a factor of 2 parallel to the y-axis. This has the effect of multiplying the y-coordinates of all points on y=f(x) by 2.

Therefore, the point (8,12) on f(x) is mapped to the point (8,2⋅12)=(8,24), and this point must lie on the graph of y=2f(x).

q-81958.name: Question 2
q-81958.problem: The point $P$ with coordinates $(10,8)$ lies on the curve $y=2f(x).$ Which of the following points must lie on $y=f(x)?$
q-81958.worked_solution:
The function $y=2f(x)$ represents a stretch of the function $y=f(x)$ by a factor of $2$ parallel to the $y$-axis. This has the effect of multiplying the $y$-coordinates of all points on $y=f(x)$ by $2.$

The point $Q(10,q)$ on $f(x)$ is mapped to the point $P(10,8)$ on $y=2f(x).$ Since we know that the $y$-coordinate of $P$ is $2$ times the $y$-coordinate of $Q,$ we can form the following equation:

$$
2q=8
$$

Solving this equation, we get $q=4.$ Therefore, the coordinates of $Q$ are $(10,4).$

The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown above. Which of the following is the graph of $y=\frac{1}{4}f(x)?$

(*Note: Figures not drawn to scale*)
q-111174.worked_solution:
To graph the function $y=\frac{1}{4}f(x),$ we take the graph of $y=f(x)$ and compress it by factor of $4$ parallel to the $y$-axis. This has the effect of dividing the $y$-coordinates of all points on $y=f(x)$ by $4.$

The resulting graph is the solid blue curve shown below.
